The Descent from the Cross

Apokathelosis · Deposition

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Mark 15:42–47

John 19:38–42

King James Version · Scripture previews

Konstantinos Kontarinis’s historic image depicts the removal of Christ’s body from the Cross. The malformed date field in its file metadata is not adopted as a precise year.

What is depicted

Figures support Christ’s body beside the Cross, with mourners below. This is the removal of the body, a distinct moment from Christ hanging on the Cross or the later Lamentation over His body.

History and tradition

And now when the even was come, because it was the preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,

Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.

And Pilate marvelled if he were already dead: and calling unto him the centurion, he asked him whether he had been any while dead.

And when he knew it of the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.

[2] Mark 15:42–45

Published explanation

And he bought fine linen, and took him down, and wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock, and rolled a stone unto the door of the sepulchre.

And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid.

The Gospel continues from the request for the body to burial. The selected image depicts the descent rather than every action in the whole passage.

[2] Mark 15:46–47
